newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador crude oil output down slightly in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador crude oil output down slightly in 1996.

text.p: Ecuadoran crude oil output fell 0.46 percent in 1996 to 140.49 million barrels because of oil pipeline problems, National Hydrocarbons Directorate said Thursday.
"The SOTE (Trans-Ecuadoran Oil Pipeline System) has deteriorated, making the transport of crude oil more difficult and putting limits on production," said a spokesman for the Directorate.

Energy Minister Alfredo Adum recently predicted that oil production would rise this year by 10,000 barrels thanks to the construction of a new pipeline by private businesses, which would mean $100 million more oil income this year.
While oil production fell to 383,858 bpd in 1996 from 386,706 bpd the previous year, there was a rise in December of 2.78 percent versus the previous month.
The official said this rise was in response to new regulations on oil output from the country's 1,335 wells.
State oil company Petroecuador released data showing that total Ecuadoran oil exports in December were 59,767 barrels. It gave no figure for the whole of 1996.
